purpose: Stop low-value high-resolution hunting and open-ended Bible cataloging. Reuse existing 266 previews and canonical catalogue to prioritize primary liturgical and devotional content.
explicitUserPriorityOrder: 1. VISUALLY_SCREEN_ALL_RELEVANT_EXISTING_WORKS for established naturalistic sacred aesthetic, respecting excluded artists
2. COVER_ALL_53_OBSERVED_CLASS_I_DATES_2026 with excellent feast/theme images, reusing same painting across octaves and related days when justified
3. COVER_MAJOR_FEASTS_NOT_CLASS_I (Candlemas, Transfiguration, Holy Rosary, Seven Sorrows, Holy Family, Holy Innocents and others in source spotlight list)
4. COVER_IMPORTANT_LOCAL_AND_TRADITIONAL_PATRONS, CORE_DOCTORS, APOSTLES_AND_EVANGELISTS from existing library first
5. BREADTH_FIRST_SCRIPTURE: Christ/NT events prioritized, fewer anchor paintings for OT, existing painting reuse and optional no-image scenes

priorityGates.aesthetic: Naturalistic figure modelling, painterly technical quality, compositional clarity, dignified religious gravity, colour and light, faithful subject; reject weak decorative/flat substitutes for major hero images. Original iconographic exceptions separately labelled.

mobileImageStandard.displayUse: Phone-first fullscreen/card/crop; original ratio preserved and full composition visible where needed.
mobileImageStandard.qualityRequirement: Enough detail to remain sharp at intended device display size; evaluate crop and colour after aesthetic selection, not before.

priorityGates.researchFreeze: Pause opportunistic new gallery research, exhaustive OT/Acts episode sourcing and jumbo master acquisition while old library Class I and primary saints remain uncurated. Do not delete previous archives.

completionSequence: Screen matching old registry images at mobile thumbnail and enlarged contain ratio; record aesthetic verdicts as PROVISIONAL, not user approvals.
Class I artwork matrix: prioritize Holy Week, Easter, Pentecost, major feasts; solve weak/unmatched cases with candidates already in registry.
Major non-Class I feast coverage: reuse strong old assets, avoid artificial daily-change quota.
Patrons, Doctors, Apostles, Evangelists: use good existing portrait, historical devotional image or documentary image when high art is unavailable; avoid forced low-quality artwork.
Only then broad NT biblical art, followed by selectively illustrated OT anchors.
Create final responsive compressed media derivatives after content and aesthetic confirmation.
notes: Thumbnail review is based on full-composition previews in generated 266-image atlas, not raw master pixels; no final work approval inferred.
Earlier fixed calendar decision is preserved even when art is unsuitable; replacement is subject to separate human review.
2026 Class I dates reflect observed 1962 local-date calendar (includes repeat octaves and Sundays). Different years move; derive dates dynamically.
St Joseph Workman and St Joseph March 19 may share Joseph subject when artistic and liturgical fit permits; do not mislabel a secular workshop painting as a specific Mass episode.
All Saints and All Souls are distinct subject themes despite neighbouring dates.

2026-10-13: additionally examined 14 already-acquired registry originals via source-complete 266-item atlas thumbnails for high-priority weak Class I feast themes. These are visually provisional candidates, no new app release or user override. Further high-quality full image review required.

existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.title: Pentecost
existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.visualNote: Salomon de Bray's Pentecost is painted in a more naturalistic, Baroque language than the older Baroncelli choice. The available thumbnail is dark and soft, so full-image detail and contrast must be checked.

existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.title: The Last Supper
existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.visualNote: Sebastiano Ricci's Last Supper has fuller figure modelling and a coherent painted interior; substantially more compatible stylistically than the historical Ugolino gold-ground panel.

existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.title: The Trinity
existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.visualNote: Hendrik van Balen's sculpturally modelled Trinity with angels is more painterly than the historical Laurent Girardin panel; detailed iconography and clarity need review.

existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.title: The Crucifixion
existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.visualNote: Pedro Orrente's Crucifixion provides serious dramatic figuration and the actual Passion subject, not the excluded El Greco Carrying the Cross. Composition is complex but credible.

existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.title: The Crucifixion
existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.visualNote: Gerard David's Crucifixion has good sacred solemnity but earlier Northern modeling; compare with Orrente on current aesthetic benchmark.

existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.title: The Crucifixion
existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.visualNote: Sodoma Crucifixion has clear full-body figure, colour and landscape; idealisation/quiet scene versus Orrente's drama to compare, not automatically promote.

existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.title: The Virgin Adoring the Host
existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.visualNote: Ingres The Virgin Adoring the Host is an accomplished devotional painting and potential Eucharistic substitute; do not claim it depicts the Corpus Christi historical liturgy.

existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.title: The Glorification of the Eucharist
existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.visualNote: Rubens Eucharistic Glorification is directly themed but a loose oil sketch, soft/low legibility at mobile sizes. Do not treat sketch as full-page painting approval.

existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.title: The Birth and Naming of Saint John the Baptist; (reverse) Trompe-l'oeil with Painting of The Man of Sorrows
existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.visualNote: Bernard van Orley's Birth and Naming of John directly matches June 24, unlike the old historical Beheading painting; Northern style but scene-specific and clearly rendered.

existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.title: The Last Judgment
existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.visualNote: Joos van Cleve Last Judgment includes Christ enthroned but is not an exact portrayal of Christ the King; useful source alternative only; mobile legibility review.

existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.title: The Annunciation
existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.visualNote: Luca Giordano Annunciation offers Baroque depth and modelling for Advent usage; preserve Champaigne Annunciation as separate first-rank selected painting.

existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.title: The Annunciation
existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.visualNote: Peter Candid Annunciation is readable, sculptural, and painterly; compare against Giordano and prior Champaigne painting, no new unique daily picture necessary.

existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.title: The Entombment
existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.visualNote: Moretto Entombment previously selected for Holy Saturday could be reused for Passion/Holy Week theme if date and iconography are kept separate.

existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.title: The Trinity Adored by All Saints
existingLibraryAlternativesScreened.visualNote: A literal all-saints assembly exists but is a complex early polyptych; not a suitable Class I primary hero under the established style. No eligible alternative yet identified inside review subset.

existingLibraryNoClearlySuitableExactHer.reason: Only already-reviewed stylized Maestro Bartolomé Entry into Jerusalem is directly tagged; allow targeted search after wider existing-art reconciliation, not a fake match.
Last Judgment provides contextual reuse but not an excellent exact King of Kings painting in screened existing subset.
Historical full-saints assembly is small/details overcrowded. Could use magnificent known saints depiction only after artistic approval; don't manufacture scenes.
